In summary, our research is concerned with

the interpretation of genetic variation at multiple sclerosis (MS) genome-wide associated locii, with the aim of highlighting the possible involvement of non-coding genetic elements in the susceptibility to MS.

the interpretation of non-coding genetic variation in MS GWAS top hits, with a particular focus on circRNAs, which have been recently implicated in a growing variety of human diseases, but not yet in MS.
the study of the genetic basis of multiple sclerosis, a complex disease with an unclear etiology and a multifactorial genetic background.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the circRNAs are not a major player in MS, but that their presence at GWAS loci is a hint for a possible involvement of the host gene in the disease.
the MS-GWAS loci are enriched for ncRNAs, especially for circular RNAs, which could represent new players in the disease pathogenesis.

circRNAs are enriched in MS-associated regions and, although their functional role in the disease is still unclear, the present results suggest a possible contribution of circRNAs in MS pathogenesis, and they pave the way to future functional studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the circRNAs are a novel class of non-coding RNA that may be involved in the susceptibility to multiple sclerosis.
the circRNAs derived in the MS-associated regions could be considered as novel candidate susceptibility genes, which should be further investigated in future functional studies.
MS-GWAs are enriched in circRNAtive elements, which may contribute to the pathogenesis of the disease, and that circRNAs can be modulated according to the genotype.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite the difficulty of interpreting GWAS results, it is possible to gain insights into non-coding elements that could be involved in disease susceptibility.
the study of non-coding variation, and in particular of ncRNAs, in the context of GWAS, should be encouraged to gain insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying complex diseases.
the interpretation of non-coding variation in GWAS loci is a promising avenue to identify new disease mechanisms.
